title: Mayor's riverboat cruise, 1924, and politicians aboard
summary: Politician Dan Jackson hired Compton to play for Mayor Big Bill Thompson on a ten-day Mississippi riverboat trip. Judge Crowe and Davey Miller were aboard; talk turns to a killing at the Pekin and its famous band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Yes, you want to get through there? I'll stop it. Okay, it's going again.
In 24, the colored political boss of the South Side, like Dawson, you've heard of Dawson there? Yes, Mr. Day. Like Dawson yesterday. His name was Dan Jackson. And stop him if you can.
That's all right. Don't worry about it. It just won't pick it up too much.

And he sent for me. He was at 34th and Michigan, his headquarters. On the southwest corner. And he sent for me. And I went down to see what he wanted. And he asked me, how would I like to play for the mayor? I said, I thought he was kidding at first. I said, how? And how? I said. So he signed me up to play for Big Bill Thompson.

It was coming up a few days or maybe weeks later. And I had to meet all these politicians. And we got the train here in Chicago and went to Alton, Illinois, by train. And when we got to Alton, there was a boat there. And the name of the boat. And the name of the boat was Cape Girardeau. Named after Missouri town.

And we got on this boat. And we got on this boat at Alton. And the boat went west to the Mississippi. And we cruised up and down the Mississippi River ten days from Peoria, Illinois, to Keokuk Island. And all the big towns like Quincy, Illinois, and St. Louis, Keokuk. And we'd stop overnight. And the boys would go out in town. So at Quincy, they all got off and went through the town. And when they come back, all the politicians had chambers, room chambers, you know. They went to a hardware store and bought all that the man had. And they came back on the boat. They had them all, it wasn't in them, but dust, because they'd never been used. And they'd never been used. And they'd all washed out. And the bartender had to fill them all with beer.
That's pretty interesting. Yeah, that handle on the side, you know.

And they were all drinking beer. I had a drummer named Sonny Christian. I don't know if you ever knew him. No, I never knew him. He was from Baltimore. So the man said, where's your, where's your, where's your, pot? Glover. He called me Glover. And I said, well, Your Honor, I haven't got any. Didn't bring me any. He said, they didn't. And I said, no, they didn't, Your Honor. So he said, well, come in and get mine. And he was over on the rails of the boat. So I left the piano, one of them got to get his. And he said, tell the bartender to rent it out and fill it up. So I took it in the bar and rent it out and I had one. And he got one for Sonny and from one of the other politicians. Judge Crowe, here, of Chicago, was State's Attorney's hand. Bob Crowe, he was a big shot then. He wasn't a big shot yet. But he was a State's Attorney's hand. Davey Miller, the prize fight referee, he was in politics. He was on that boat. He was Hachimilla's brother. Hachimilla got killed in the Pekin one, I think.
I heard there was some killing down there at the Pekin once. Yeah, Hachimilla. I think Joe Oliver was playing there then, I believe somebody told me. Joe Oliver's band was working.
There were so many different bands who played upstairs. The Pekin band was famous. Do you remember? The Pekin?
I mean combination. Well, that's alright. If you want to get your voice on here, it's alright too. Simon Stewart, yeah.
